header: Date: 2025-06-03 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Ridgeway VP Eng), Erin Zhao (Ridgeway SRE), David Mills (Ridgeway Security)
summary: Follow-up on last week's production incident impacting inference tail-latency during heavy KV-cache churn. Reviewed RCA drafts, mitigations pushed to canary, outstanding runbook gaps, and next steps for a controlled canary + rollback window. Customer emphasized auditability and KMS changes; Redwood to deliver runbook patch and load-test artifacts.
topics: RCA review: root causes and contributing factors
Mitigation status: hotfixes, cache tuning, autoscaler behavior
Canary rollout plan and success criteria
transcript: [00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know this is the Ridgeway reliability follow-up — want to make sure we cover the RCAs and actionable mitigations. Samir, Erin — can you confirm the priority?

[00:12] Samir Patel: Yeah, thanks. Priority is high. The spike last Thursday impacted a handful of customer-facing flows, particularly loan-quote generation. We lost about 9% of requests breaching the 500ms SLO for a ~30 minute window.

[00:28] Erin Zhao: Quick correction — it was actually 7.8% by our dashboards, but there was a sustained tail. We saw KV cache thrash when drifted keys hit a blob of cold states. Also autoscaler reacted late under the 2 min window.

[00:45] Marcus Chen: Got it. From Redwood's side our preliminary timeline shows a confluence: new client-side pattern created high prefix variance, which prevented effective prefix caching, plus a rare GC pause on one node and then the autoscaler single-step growth. Together that caused request queuing and higher p99 latency.

[01:10] David Mills: On the security side we checked logs — nothing suspicious; it looks operational. But we need better audit trails in case we have to show regulators; can you outline what logs you'll be delivering?
[01:22] Lena Ortiz: Yes — we'll provide the request-id chain, per-token cost traces, and the kv-cache hit/miss timeline. Marcus, can you call out what will be in the runbook?

[01:30] Marcus Chen: Sure — runbook will include: immediate mitigation (cache key normalization toggle), fallback route to lower-memory model variant, how to drain and reprovision the problematic pod, and rollback steps. We'll include exact CLI commands and synthetic test harness commands. Note: the cache key normalization is a config flip; it doesn't require redeploy.
[02:05] Erin Zhao: That normalization toggle — is it guaranteed safe? We worry about correctness at the app layer if keys mutate semantics.

[02:12] Marcus Chen: Good point. It's safe for our recommended patterns; it rewrites client prefixes to a stable canonical form. We'll include a verification test that asserts no semantics change for our typical prompts. But we'll call out caveats in the runbook for custom tokenization.
[03:00] Samir Patel: The autoscaler behavior was a surprise. Our expectation was incremental scaling; we saw it step twice and still lag. Is Redwood changing scaling policies server-side?

[03:12] Lena Ortiz: We have an interim change pushed to canary to shorten the scale-up cooldown and to allow faster ramp for short bursts. That helps with throughput but could increase cost; we'll measure impact in the canary window.
[03:40] Marcus Chen: Also added proactive pre-warming for sequences over 1024 tokens and improved KV-caching heuristics that reduce prefix churn. Those are on the canary cluster now.
[04:05] Erin Zhao: Can we see the canary logs and the exact dashboard widgets? We need to show our execs the before/after numbers for p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta.

[04:18] Lena Ortiz: Yup — will share a dashboard snapshot link and a csv export. Postmortem doc will include before/after charts. Draft link: https://redwood.app/links/ridgeway-postmortem-2025 (internal).
[05:00] David Mills: KMS — we need the logs to be encrypted with our key and rotated per policy. Is the canary using customer-managed key?

[05:12] Marcus Chen: Canary uses Redwood-managed KMS currently. For the production rollout we can switch to customer-managed CMK; the team will provide the policy steps. We'll include the KMS integration checklist in the runbook.
[06:30] Erin Zhao: About the root cause doc — you mentioned GC pause and autoscaler together. Is the GC pause an env issue or workload? We want to know if this is likely to recur.

[06:45] Marcus Chen: The GC pause was due to a non-heap resource compaction that coincided with high concurrent KV misses. It's low probability but not zero. Mitigation: container memory tuning and a soft cap to avoid large compactions during high QPS.
[08:00] Samir Patel: Ok let's go through the timeline checkpoints in the RCA. Can you capture exact timestamps we can map to our logs?
[08:10] Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a table with event timestamps (ingest arrival rates, cache hit/miss spikes, pod restarts). Also include a list of correlated request IDs.
[09:40] Erin Zhao: One more ask — please surface which customers were impacted (anonymized) and which routes. We have contractual notif requirements within 72 hours for P2 incidents.
[09:55] Lena Ortiz: Understood. We'll produce an anonymized list and the incident notification note. Priya, team will coordinate legal/comms?
[10:05] Priya Kapoor: I'll draft the comms and align with Ridgeway's CLM. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

[11:20] Marcus Chen: Regarding long-term reliability improvements, we recommended: stronger prefix canonicalization, a TTL-based KV eviction policy tuned to common workload patterns, and a more conservative autoscaler profile for production tenants with strict SLOs.
[12:00] Samir Patel: TTL eviction could help but we need to be careful about bursty workloads that rely on long-lived cached entries. Can we do a hybrid policy?
[12:10] Marcus Chen: Yes — hybrid policy with per-route overrides. We'll deliver sample policies keyed by route name and expected sequence length distribution.
[13:30] Erin Zhao: Monitoring — can we get finer-grained KV metrics? Right now our dashboard only shows cluster-level hit-rate. We want per-route and per-model metrics to triage in future.
[13:42] Lena Ortiz: Already on the roadmap. For the canary we'll expose per-route kv_hit_rate, avg_key_size, and miss latency. We'll add alert thresholds tied to p99 latency and queue depth.
[15:00] David Mills: On auditability — we need immutable logs for the window of the incident. Can you confirm retention and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM?
[15:12] Marcus Chen: Yes, logs can be exported via S3 with server-side encryption using your CMK. We'll include the transfer playbook.
[16:30] Erin Zhao: One friction we had during the incident was not being able to quickly toggle the fallback to lower-cost model variant. Is that something you can make a one-click option in Console?
[16:42] Lena Ortiz: Good product feedback. We can add a pre-flight toggle for fallbacks in the console; for now Marcus will provide the CLI command and a runbook section for it.
[18:00] Samir Patel: Let's define success criteria for the canary: 1) p99 <= 450ms for 95% of traffic over 1 hour, 2) no >2% increase in per-token cost, 3) all audit logs present and encrypted.
[18:20] Marcus Chen: Agreed. We'll instrument the canary to fail fast if thresholds breach, and automatic rollback will kick in if p99 > 500ms for a sustained 5 minute window.
[20:00] Erin Zhao: What about test coverage — will Redwood re-run the failing synthetic tests that exposed the issue?
[20:12] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we'll run the synthetic harness against canary and staging and share the results. Marcus will attach the script.

[22:00] Samir Patel: Cost — if this requires a sustained increase in capacity that's fine short-term, but we need visibility on the monthly delta. We'll need an estimate before we sign off on a permanent autoscaler change.
[22:12] Marcus Chen: We'll include an estimated cost delta for several autoscaler profiles — conservative, moderate, aggressive — and the incremental cost of pre-warming.
[25:00] Erin Zhao: One more security question: during the canary, who has permission to flip the normalization toggle? We want RBAC controls to be explicit.
[25:12] David Mills: We'll need at least two approvers for production toggles per our compliance rules.
[25:30] Lena Ortiz: We'll include the RBAC checklist and a recommended approver flow. For now canary toggles will be limited to Ridgeway ops and Redwood site-ops with audit logs.
[28:00] Marcus Chen: Quick note — we've already pushed a minor patch to reduce KV lock contention; this is low-risk and can be rolled back instantly. That lives in canary cluster now.
[30:00] Erin Zhao: Ok please send the exact git SHA and the patch notes so our engineers can review.
[30:12] Lena Ortiz: Will do. Action item on Lena to share the patch link, Marcus to share load-test harness, and Priya to coordinate comms.
[35:00] Samir Patel: Any outstanding unknowns? I want a concise list for our exec summary.

[35:10] Marcus Chen: Unknowns: exact probability of GC pause recurrence under differing memory configs, and how third-party client patterns might create new prefix churn — both are solvable but need testing.
[37:00] Erin Zhao: We'll run a focused stress test with our exact production traffic replay and share results back with Redwood in two business days.
[37:12] Lena Ortiz: Great. We'll reconvene after the staging failover test and before the canary rollout — propose 2025-06-11 for a 30-minute sync.
[37:30] Samir Patel: That works. Make sure the agenda is tight: canary criteria, rollback commands, and comms draft.
[40:00] Priya Kapoor: I'll create the calendar invite and include the runbook draft and the CSV of impacted request-ids.
[41:00] Erin Zhao: One small note — include a short blurb in the runbook about customer-notification time windows and legal triggers. We need to be compliant.
[42:30] Lena Ortiz: Acknowledged. We'll also add an appendix describing the root-cause signal chain so auditors can follow the technical narrative.
[45:00] David Mills: On the audit appendix, please include hashed request ids and a verification script so we can independently verify integrity.
[46:12] Marcus Chen: We'll include a hash mapping and verification steps; that will require a short HMAC key exchange — we'll coordinate securely.
[50:00] Samir Patel: Final recap please — who does what and by when?

[50:10] Lena Ortiz: Recap: Lena send runbook + patch link (due 6/5), Marcus send load tests + tuning guide (due 6/7), Erin run staging failover (target 6/10), Priya draft customer comms (EOD 6/4). We schedule follow-up 6/11 30-min. Any additions?
[50:35] Erin Zhao: Add: confirm CMK access and log export config (Erin) — due 6/6.
[51:00] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[51:10] Lena Ortiz: Thanks — we'll push the runbook and links after the call. Bye.
[62:00] (call ended)
Notes: transcript contains some automated transcript noise; proper, cleaned postmortem will be delivered in the shared doc.
